info.title: HNN Biller — Master Control API (SaaS owner)
info.description:
Manage every organisation on the deployment — clients, payers, EMR/EHR partners — the IT leads assigned to them, and each client’s edition. **This is the transition API: move any client between commercial and non-commercial instantly, in both directions, with no data loss.**

### Editions
Every client runs on one of two editions in the **same deployment**:

| Edition | Includes |
|---|---|
| `non_commercial` | Billing, payer routing, patient payments, dashboard, notifications, medical reports |
| `commercial` | Everything above **plus** revenue rules & other charges, financing, NHIS ClaimIt tracker, agnostic payer tabs, audit ledger |

Switching is a per-client flag flip — no redeploy, no data migration, and **nothing is deleted on downgrade**.
Commercial-only endpoints return **402 `upgrade_required`** when the caller's client is non-commercial.
Check your own entitlement any time with `GET /api/v1/bills/edition`.

**Base URL:** `https://nextgenhnnbiller-production.up.railway.app`

_The platform never custodies funds: money moves account-to-account to the provider; fees are accrued to the ledger as receivables._

Counts across the deployment
All clients with edition + feature map
get.description: Each client's verificationChannels ({ sms, whatsapp, includeTreatmentDetail }) is included in the listing — all false unless set via PUT .../verification-channels below. Each client's messagingCredentials (its own bring-your-own-credentials provider account, if any) is included too, masked to { provider, configured, hint, useOwnCredentials, updatedAt } — see the Messaging endpoints below.

post.summary: Create a client (returns its tenant API key)

put.summary: Transition a client between editions (both directions)
put.description: Instant, reversible, non-destructive. Downgrading stops serving commercial features but retains all data; upgrading again restores full access to it.

put.summary: Turn on SMS and/or WhatsApp delivery of the patient verification message for this client
put.description: Off for every channel by default. When a channel is on, the same verification link sent automatically at billing time (and on resend) also goes out on that channel, with a one-time reply code the patient can text back instead of opening the link — see the Core Billing API's inbound webhook (/api/v1/webhooks/messaging-inbound). includeTreatmentDetail is a separate opt-in, off by default, for whether the message also lists the treatment/line items; left off, the message carries only the amount and the link, consistent with this platform's no-PHI-over-SMS/WhatsApp default. Real delivery now runs through Twilio, Africa's Talking, or Hubtel, resolved per send — this client's own credentials if it has turned on bring-your-own-credentials, else the platform-wide test account if HNN has activated one, else sandbox (log only) — see the Messaging endpoints below. Turning a channel on here is safe before any provider is configured or activated — nothing sends for real until the server also has MESSAGING_SANDBOX set to false and a usable provider resolves for this client.

get.summary: Wired-in SMS/WhatsApp providers, their required fields, and WhatsApp support
get.description: Twilio, Africa's Talking and Hubtel are all wired in; this lists each one's field names for the credentials object used by the two endpoints below (e.g. Twilio needs accountSid, authToken, from), plus an honest per-provider whatsapp status — supported, unverified (documented behaviour not yet confirmed against a live account from this deployment), or unsupported (the provider has no WhatsApp product at all, e.g. Hubtel). encryptionConfigured reports whether the server has a CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY set; saving any credentials below fails with 422 until it does.

get.summary: Current state of the platform-wide shared test account (masked)
get.description: One shared Twilio/Africa's Talking/Hubtel account HNN can activate for a live test and deactivate again when done, used by any client below that hasn't turned on its own bring-your-own-credentials. Never returns the encrypted blob or the raw secret — only provider, configured, a last-4-chars hint, active, and updatedAt.

put.summary: Configure and/or activate or deactivate the platform-wide shared test account
put.description: Body { provider?, credentials?, active? }. provider is one of twilio, africastalking, hubtel — see GET .../messaging/providers for each one's field names. Omit credentials to change only active (the deactivate-when-testing-is-over switch) without resupplying the secret; include it to set or replace what's stored — doing so for a provider other than the one already saved clears the old encrypted blob first, so the UI never shows "configured" with a hint for a different provider's secret. Rejects (422 no_credentials_configured) any call that would leave active:true with no usable provider+credentials pair, including a bare provider switch with no new credentials while still active — send active:false (or the new credentials) explicitly instead. This sits underneath the server's own MESSAGING_SANDBOX switch — while that is true, nothing here is ever actually sent, active account or not.

credentials.description: Raw provider fields (e.g. accountSid/authToken/from for twilio) — see GET .../messaging/providers. Stored encrypted; never echoed back.

put.summary: Configure a client's own "bring your own credentials" provider account
put.description: Body { useOwnCredentials?, provider?, credentials? }. When useOwnCredentials is true and a provider + credentials are saved, this client's own Twilio/Africa's Talking/Hubtel account is used for every send instead of the platform's shared test account above — it always wins when on. Same provider list, field names, encryption, and masking as the platform test-account endpoint; see GET .../messaging/providers. Switching provider without new credentials in the same call clears the old encrypted blob rather than keeping it stored under the new provider's name. Rejects (422 no_credentials_configured) turning useOwnCredentials on with no usable provider+credentials pair saved. Master Control is where this is entered on the client's behalf today; nothing about the storage or sending logic is specific to who calls it.

credentials.description: Raw provider fields — see GET .../messaging/providers. Stored encrypted; never echoed back.

200.description: { id, messagingCredentials: { provider, configured, hint, useOwnCredentials, updatedAt } }

get.summary: Live sandbox/live state of both rails (Settlement + Messaging)
get.description: The runtime-authoritative switch. SBG_SANDBOX/MESSAGING_SANDBOX only seed the starting default the first time this is read with nothing saved yet (seededFromEnv: true in the response). Once anything here has been saved via the PUT below, this record governs at runtime, independent of those env vars, until a restart with an empty database. The two rails are switched independently, which is what makes a hybrid deployment possible — e.g. Messaging live while Settlement stays sandboxed for further testing, or vice versa.

200.description: { settlement: { sandbox }, messaging: { sandbox }, updatedAt, updatedBy, seededFromEnv }

put.summary: Switch Settlement and/or Messaging between sandbox and live
put.description: Body { settlement?: { sandbox }, messaging?: { sandbox }, confirm? }. Only the rail(s) actually included are changed; the other keeps whatever it currently resolves to. Switching settlement.sandbox to false (live) moves real money through Stanbic for every payer with settlement credentials configured, so it requires confirm set to exactly "LIVE" (case-sensitive) in the same call — otherwise this returns 422 confirmation_required and nothing is changed. Messaging has no such requirement in either direction, since going live there only costs SMS/WhatsApp send fees, not bank risk. Switching either rail back to sandbox never requires confirm.

confirm.description: Must be exactly "LIVE" when switching settlement.sandbox to false; ignored otherwise

422.description: confirmation_required — switching Settlement to live without confirm:"LIVE"

get.summary: Global payers, with edition, commission and settlement-credentials state
get.description: Each payer's commercial edition and licence state is included (edition, editionUpdatedAt, licence — see the Editions endpoints), its per-claim commission masked to { enabled, rate, cap, updatedAt } (see PUT .../commission), and its Stanbic/SBG settlement credentials masked to { configured, hint, updatedAt, updatedBy } plus legacySettlementCredentialsConfigured, which is true when an older plaintext payer.sbg credential is what's actually in effect because nothing's been saved via PUT .../settlement-credentials yet.

post.summary: Create an insurer or corporate payer (returns its payer key)

put.summary: Transition a payer between editions (both directions)
put.description: Instant, reversible, non-destructive — mirrors PUT .../clients/{id}/edition. Unlike a hospital client, a payer's edition does not gate its own feature access (NNEST, price lists, targets, prior approvals keep working regardless of edition); it only gates whether the per-claim commission below can be enabled.

put.summary: Set a commercial payer's per-claim platform commission
put.description: Body { enabled?, rate? } — either alone leaves the other untouched. rate accepts 0..1 or 0..100 and is clamped to 15%. This commission is separate from, and additional to, whatever expedited-settlement fee a hospital's own pricing rules may already charge this same payer (see the Core Billing API's revenue rules) — both can accrue on the same settled claim. Returns 402 upgrade_required if the payer is not currently commercial; upgrade it first via PUT .../edition.

200.description: { payerId, commission: { enabled, rate, updatedAt, updatedBy }, cap }

post.summary: Renew a payer's licence for another term (default 6 months)
post.description: Mirrors POST .../clients/{id}/renew. Extends from the later of now or current expiry. feeAmount records what was charged (0 while free).

200.description: { payerId, name, edition, expiresAt, termMonths, feeAmount, key }

put.summary: Set a payer's Stanbic/SBG marketplace username/password (encrypted at rest)
put.description: Body { username, password }, both required. Used to authorise the A2A transfer to a provider — see services/settlement.js#clientForPayer() in the Core Billing API. Stored encrypted the same way SMS/WhatsApp provider credentials are (CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY must be set on the server); never echoed back, only masked as { configured, hint, updatedAt, updatedBy }. Falls back to a legacy plaintext credential already on the payer record whenever nothing's saved here — see legacySettlementCredentialsConfigured on GET .../payers.

200.description: { payerId, settlementCredentials: { configured, hint, updatedAt, updatedBy } }

delete.summary: Clear a payer's encrypted settlement credentials
delete.description: Reverts to whatever legacy plaintext payer.sbg credential exists on the record, or none at all.

get.summary: SaaS-wide accrued revenue (all clients), by type, by client and by payer
get.description: Aggregates platform_fee_* ledger entries across every tenant. All figures are accrued receivables, not cash held. byPayer[] attributes expedited-settlement and per-claim commission fees to the payer that owes them (derived from the fee's own refs, not from the bill's coverage, which can be imprecise for a split bill); a fee type with no payer in its refs — e.g. a report fee charged to the patient — is simply left out of byPayer, not dumped under an "unknown" bucket.

put.summary: Set licensing policy (free vs licensed, term, fee)
put.description: mode free_non_commercial = fee-free (default). mode licensed = require a live licence; set licenseFee per term. Switching to free forces the fee to zero. Switching to licensed starts a one-off grace window (default 30 days) during which clients without a licence keep working.

graceDays.description: grace window for unlicensed clients after switching to licensed

post.summary: Upload a payer pre-approved price list (CSV text)
post.description: Body { csv, replace? }. CSV columns: code, name, price [, unit, provider, category]. A provider (tenant id or facility name) sets a facility-specific price; blank rows are the payer default.

csv.description: Raw CSV text (Excel exported to CSV works)

get.summary: Get a payer price list (or search with q)

200.description: { count, uploadedAt, sample[] } or { data[] } when q set

put.summary: Toggle whether a payer’s price list governs settlement (default off)
put.description: When enabled, claims routed to this payer are repriced to its approved prices (facility-specific first, then default, else the billed price). The patient absorbs any gap between billed and approved. Default off = the list is reference-only and the billed price governs.

put.summary: Toggle whether this payer requires the patient to verify their bill first (default off)
put.description: When enabled, POST …/authorize (Payer API or secure claim link) is refused with 409 patient_verification_pending until the patient confirms via the link sent automatically when the bill was created. A missing or disputed verification counts the same as pending. See the Payer & Claims API.
